newsitem.title: USA: CUC to acquire Hebdo Mag Int'l in $440 mln stock swap.
newsitem.headline: CUC to acquire Hebdo Mag Int'l in $440 mln stock swap.

text.p: CUC International Inc. said on Thursday it would acquire Hebdo Mag International Inc., a Paris-based international publisher and distributor of classified advertising, in a stock swap valued at $440 million.
CUC is expected to close an $11 billion merger with HFS Inc., a rapidly expanding real estate and travel services company, in the fall.

"With CUC's existing consumer services and HFS's preferred alliances, we will now be able to leverage our direct-marketing expertise to cross-sell complementary services, such as AutoVantage, to someone buying a car," said CUC Chairman Walter Forbes.
CUC said it intends to account for the aquisition of the privately held Hebdo Mag as a pooling of interests.
Hebdo Mag managers and founders Louise T. Blouin MacBain and John H. MacBain will continue to manage the business and be "significant long-term shareholders" in CUC, the company said.

Hebdo Mag has operations in 12 countries, including Canada, France, Sweden, Hungary, the United States, Italy, Russia, and Holland. The company publishes over 150 titles in 12 countries on 3 continents.

CUC International is a membership-based, consumer services company that currently provides access to travel, shopping, auto, dining, financial, and other services to more than 68 million consumers worldwide through its more than 20 membership programs.
CUC International expects the acquisition to slightly increase its 1997 earnings.
Its stock was up 31 cents at $26.69 a share on the New York Stock Exchange.
